trajectory_summary: The call opens hostile over contact frequency and spends nearly the entire runtime managing scam/legitimacy suspicion rather than building toward genuine interest in solar. The rep survives through persistence, micro-trades (marking her off contact lists), and eventual disclosure of her own knowledge limits, landing a conditional appointment that the customer frames as reversible and trust-contingent.
outcome_dispute: The v1 tag is unknown; observed outcome is a tentative, fragile booking rather than a clean booked appointment — the customer's closing line ('if you're not on the line, I'm hanging up') and repeated conditional framing throughout make this a conditional_booking, not a stable win.

observed_outcome.quote: Sweet, Ashley. I'm super excited to see what we can do here. And, again, let me know if there's anything I can do on my end, but we'll plan on Monday 10/30.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day and time (Monday 10:30) is agreed and confirmed at the end of the call, but it is booked under explicit customer conditions (rep must be on the line, spouse excluded, 'if I decide I don't wanna do this I would love it if y'all would stop trying to contact me') that make it structurally fragile rather than a clean, stable booking.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captures the $262/month figure and reacts ('Holy smokes') but never returns to it as leverage — later, when the customer raises the cost-skepticism objection at 16:57 ('saving me a electric bill does not pay for a solar panel'), the rep responds with her personal motivation instead of flipping back to the $262 figure as the actual expense being replaced.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never asks a version of 'what interested you in solar' — the call opens straight into the affordability objection and the bill-swap explanation, so no interest reason is ever captured or available to use.

key_moments.stewart_read: Rep gives out her personal number to secure the bill photo, a classic anti-pattern flagged in the schema as a privacy/scale exposure workaround.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. I mean, looking at the home itself, you get really good sun exposure. Right? Like, you're you're basically getting blasted with sun all day. So I think the system would really produce well.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep notices strong sun exposure and reflects it back as a positive production signal, which is a legitimate anchor point the closer can build on.

key_moments.quote: It's all about lowering the power bills for me. That's why I am in this position that I'm in.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer just said saving on the electric bill 'does not pay for a solar panel' and something 'doesn't add up' — a clear cost-skepticism trigger for the flip (what's expensive is staying on the current bill), but the rep responds with a values statement about her own motivation instead of inverting the objection.
